reasoning: CHD4 is a core subunit of the NuRD chromatin‑remodeling complex that functions mainly as a transcriptional repressor by recruiting HDAC activity to target promoters. Loss of this repressive scaffold generally leads to increased histone acetylation and Pol II activity at genes normally kept silent, and CHD4 knock‑down in macrophages has been shown to de‑repress multiple LPS‑induced inflammatory genes. Applying the scaffold‑repressor rule (Section 2.6), the knockout of CHD4 is expected to relieve repression of the C‑type lectin gene Clec4d, resulting in its up‑regulation.
